nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: A yard with a court painted on it, a climbing frame, a bench, and a shed at the side. The gate you came through is behind you.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: There is nobody here and nothing in the yard asks you to stand anywhere in particular.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: You reached the open yard behind the estate: a court two hoops wide, a shed, a bench, a climbing frame.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: Behind the shed the fence has a gap in it, and the ground past the gap is the same concrete as the yard.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The equipment shed has a green door, a hasp, and a padlock hanging from the hasp. The sheet taped inside the window faces out.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You could put a hand on the door. You could read the sheet. You could walk on.

choices.text: Try the door against its frame.
Read the sheet in the window.

nodes.speaker: voice_boundary
nodes.text: Let me feel how it sits.

nodes.speaker: voice_boundary
nodes.text: The door is not swollen. The opening is wider than the door on the hinge side. Something was taken out of this frame and nobody put it back.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The shed door swings in: the padlock is shut around empty air and the hasp is held by nothing.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: Chairs stacked to the ceiling, a coiled rope, three broken shuttlecocks. On the top chair, taped under the seat where nobody sitting would see it, a name in marker.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You cannot read it from the doorway. You would have to move the stack, and the stack is the only thing in the shed holding the stack up.

nodes.speaker: voice_boundary
nodes.text: Two fingers, maybe three. The frame is wider than the door. That gap should not be there.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The door does not move. There is daylight under it, and the paint behind the hasp is clean, as if the hasp had been somewhere else for a long time.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The shed door does not close flush. The paint behind the hasp is clean and the hasp is screwed in crooked.

nodes.speaker: voice_ledger
nodes.text: Rows. Let me have the rows.

nodes.speaker: voice_ledger
nodes.text: Nine periods. The hand gets smaller as it goes down. The last two rows are the same day written twice, and the second one is dated next week.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The duty sheet in the shed window lists the same day twice; the second copy is dated next week.

nodes.speaker: voice_ledger
nodes.text: Nine. Nine rows, nine periods. Nine is the number of rows.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You count them again and get eight. Rain has run two rows together. One name is still legible, and it is the surname chalked on the wall at the mouth of the alley.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The duty sheet has been rained on. One surname on it is also chalked on the alley wall.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You leave the padlock hanging. Behind you the hoop on the near side has no net, and the one at the far end does.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: A table-tennis ball is wedged between the shed's footing and the concrete. Under the hedge behind it there is something pale and flat.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The gap goes back further than the ball does.

nodes.speaker: voice_boundary
nodes.text: Fingers first. I will tell you where the back of it is.

nodes.speaker: voice_boundary
nodes.text: A hand deep, then concrete, then a lip. There is a ledge behind the ball. Something on the ledge is not round.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: Behind the ball, on a ledge under the shed, there is a flat metal tag with a hole in one end.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The tag is cold and blank on one side. On the other side there is a stamped number, four digits, and the paint in the digits is the same green as the shed door.

nodes.speaker: voice_boundary
nodes.text: There is nothing behind it. The gap is a hand deep and then it closes.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: Your knuckles scrape and the ball shifts and settles again. The pale thing under the hedge is not behind the ball at all. It is further out, and it is a strip of white paint on a stick.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The ball stays wedged. The shed has two footings and the gap is only on one side.

nodes.speaker: voice_ledger
nodes.text: Shadow first. Shadow is cheaper than knuckles.

nodes.speaker: voice_ledger
nodes.text: The shadow is longer than the gap. Whatever is under the hedge is nearer to you than the ball is, and it is the wrong shape for a ball.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The pale thing under the hedge sits nearer than the wedged ball, so it is not the ball's shadow.

nodes.speaker: voice_ledger
nodes.text: One gap, one ball, one shadow. It balances.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: It balances and tells you nothing. The ball stays where it is. The shed has two footings and the gap is only on the left one, which is the kind of thing you notice when a sum has just failed you.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The sums balanced and told you nothing. The shed has two footings and the gap is only on the left one.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You leave the ball where it is. It is not yours, and nobody in this yard is waiting for it.
